extracted.intended_audience: Employees of the United States Patent and Trademark Office (including political appointees, SES, attorneys, and other staff)
extracted.subtask_description: A concise summary of the ethics rules and standards that USPTO employees must follow, covering general ethical principles, conflicts of interest (financial and personal), outside activities, political activity, gifts, use of government resources, seeking employment, post‑employment restrictions, and financial disclosure obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public service is a public trust
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees are placed in a position of trust and must place loyalty to the Constitution, the laws, and ethical principles above private gain; comply with Government ethics rules during and in some cases after service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Familiarize yourself with federal conflict of interest statutes, the Standards of Ethical Conduct, and Department of Commerce policies; consult an ethics official for specific situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: General ethical principle — no conflicting financial interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees shall not hold financial interests that conflict with the conscientious performance of duty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a conflict exists, disqualify from participating in the matter unless an exemption applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: General ethical principle — no using nonpublic information for private gain
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees shall not engage in financial transactions using nonpublic Government information or allow improper use of such information to further any private interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not trade or advise others based on nonpublic data obtained through Government work.

rubrics_metrics.name: General ethical principle — gift rules and solicitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees shall not, except as permitted in ethics regulations, solicit or accept any gift or other item of monetary value from persons/entities seeking official action or regulated by the agency or whose interests may be affected by an employee's duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the Gifts section for exceptions, thresholds, and reporting requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: General ethical principle — honest effort
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees shall put forth honest effort in the performance of their duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: General ethical principle — no unauthorized commitments
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees shall not knowingly make unauthorized commitments or promises purporting to bind the Government.

rubrics_metrics.name: General ethical principle — no use of public office for private gain
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees shall not use public office for private gain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes use of authority, contacts, or title for personal benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: General ethical principle — impartiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees shall act impartially and not give preferential treatment to any private organization or individual.

rubrics_metrics.name: General ethical principle — protect federal property
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees shall protect and conserve Federal property and shall not use it for other than authorized activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: General ethical principle — avoid incompatible outside employment
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees shall not engage in outside employment or activities, including seeking or negotiating for employment, that conflict with official Government duties and responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek ethics advice about specific outside employment to ensure compatibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: General ethical principle — disclose waste/fraud/abuse
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees shall disclose waste, fraud, abuse, and corruption to appropriate authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office of Inspector General hotline and procedures are available for filing complaints.

rubrics_metrics.name: General ethical principle — fulfill obligations as citizens
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees shall satisfy in good faith obligations as citizens, including financial obligations such as taxes.

rubrics_metrics.name: General ethical principle — equal opportunity laws
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees shall adhere to laws and regulations that provide equal opportunity regardless of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, or handicap.

rubrics_metrics.name: General ethical principle — avoid appearance of impropriety
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees shall endeavor to avoid actions creating the appearance that they are violating the law or ethical standards; appearance is judged from the perspective of a reasonable person with knowledge of the facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When in doubt about appearances, consult an ethics official or supervisor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial conflicts of interest — general disqualification rule
rubrics_metrics.description: You cannot participate in a matter that will have a direct and predictable effect on your financial interests or the financial interests of covered relatives/household members, business partners, outside employers, prospective employers, or organizations in which you serve as trustee/officer/board member.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When such a conflict exists, you must disqualify yourself from the matter unless an applicable exemption applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial conflicts — exceptions for certain holdings
rubrics_metrics.description: Participation may be permitted if the financial interest is: a holding in a publicly-traded diversified mutual fund; less than $50,000 in a publicly-traded sector-specific mutual fund; publicly-traded stock/bond holdings of $15,000 or less in a company; or publicly-traded stock/bond holdings of $25,000 or less for participation in broad policy matters (with sector totals $50,000 or less).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waivers (conflict of interest waivers) are generally available only in unusual circumstances or for employees serving overseas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on USPTO employees obtaining patent rights
rubrics_metrics.description: You are barred by statute from applying for or acquiring (except by inheritance/bequest) any right or interest in a patent issued by USPTO while employed by USPTO and for one year thereafter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of insider information and IPO investing restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: You are barred from using insider information to make investment decisions; if you file a public financial disclosure report you are barred from investing in Initial Public Offerings (IPOs) except as available to the public generally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts based on personal relationships — general disqualification
rubrics_metrics.description: You cannot participate in a matter in which a person with whom you have a 'covered relationship' is before the Government if your participation would cause a reasonable person to question your impartiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covered relationships include a variety of personal and professional connections (see covered relationships entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Covered relationships — who is included
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons with whom you have a 'covered relationship' include: persons with whom you have or are seeking business or financial relationships; household members; close relatives; employers and clients of your spouse/parents/dependent children (and prospective employers/clients); recent former non‑Federal employers/clients (within past year, or two years for political appointees); and organizations in which you are an active participant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you are a political appointee who served as a registered lobbyist or foreign agent in the two years prior to appointment, you cannot participate in matters you lobbied on or in related issue areas for two years after appointment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict-based-on-relationship exceptions (waiver)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Government's need for your participation outweighs appearance concerns, a waiver of the disqualification may be available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact an ethics official for guidance and to request any waiver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perception concerns beyond covered relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if no legal disqualification applies (e.g., matters involving a personal friend), you should discuss perception concerns with your supervisor who may reassign the matter on management grounds; you may also consult an ethics official.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reassignment can be done without a legal disqualification or providing detailed explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outside activities — general compatibility requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Outside jobs, positions in non‑Federal organizations, and personal activities during non‑duty hours must be compatible with Government duties; activities that conflict with performance or create an appearance of misuse of office are prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If outside activity would require disqualification that prevents performance of important USPTO duties, it may be incompatible; seek advice from an ethics official.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outside practice of law — limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Most pro bono activities are allowed if the client has no matters before your office and the matter is not one in which the U.S. Government has an interest; generally you may not provide legal services regarding obtaining a patent or copyright or concerning the validity of a patent or registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attorneys should consult applicable bar rules and federal ethics rules; other situations decided case-by-case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching, speaking, and writing restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: You cannot receive payments (other than travel) for teaching, speaking, or writing in your personal capacity about Department programs/operations unless the teaching is in regular curriculum of an accredited school; writings about USPTO programs related to your duties must be given to your supervisor for prior review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SES political appointees must receive prior approval from an ethics official before teaching for compensation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working for a foreign government and registration restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Employment with, providing services to, or accepting compensation from a foreign government is prohibited by the Emoluments Clause unless expressly permitted by statute; you also cannot engage in activities requiring registration under FARA or LDA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule on contacting Government and receiving payments for others' communications
rubrics_metrics.description: In your personal capacity you generally cannot act as an agent/attorney or be paid to communicate with a Federal agency or court to influence Government action on behalf of someone else, including relatives, friends, clients, or an employer, unless an exception applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies during and after Government service for certain periods; payments based on representational activities before a Federal agency while you served are also barred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to contacting the Government rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Permitted representations include: (1) representing parents/spouse/children/estate/trust or someone for whom you have power of attorney with prior approval from an ethics official; (2) representing other Federal employees in some personnel disputes if unpaid; and (3) representing a professional/recreational group whose membership is mostly federal employees regarding matters not involving claims against the Government or Government financial benefits, if unpaid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approval from an ethics official may be required for some exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serving on nonprofit boards in official capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: You may serve as a board member/officer/agency liaison with a nonprofit as part of USPTO duties without disqualification for matters where the organization has a financial interest, but such service requires senior agency official approval and consideration of mission appropriateness and resource availability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organization documents may be subject to FOIA; anti‑lobbying, Hatch Act, and fundraising restrictions still apply; contact ethics official for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on noncareer SES employees' outside income and activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Noncareer SES political appointees may not receive earned income greater than $29,895 per year, any compensation for fiduciary professional practice or affiliation with such a firm, or serve as an officer or on a board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are special ethics restrictions for noncareer SES appointees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political activities — general prohibitions
rubrics_metrics.description: You must keep Government activities separate from political activities and may not engage in partisan political activities on Government premises, while on official duty, solicit or accept political contributions, invite or host political fund‑raisers, use Government position to support/opppose a party or candidate, use Government equipment or resources for partisan political activities, run as a party‑identified candidate (with limited local exceptions), or ask for/accept volunteer services from a subordinate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are narrow exceptions (e.g., certain union solicitations) — consult ethics guidance for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political activities — permitted personal time activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Except where restricted (and subject to career SES rules), during non‑duty hours employees may give funds to candidates/parties, attend political fund‑raisers or rallies, assist in campaign management, serve as officers in political groups, solicit votes, make phone calls or stuff envelopes, and speak at political events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some activities (noted with asterisks in the source) are not permitted for career SES members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career SES special political restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Career SES members cannot actively assist in partisan campaigns or be officers in political organizations even during non‑duty hours, though they can vote, give money, display signs, and attend political events; they may also participate in nonpartisan elections and referenda.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gifts — prohibition on bribes and outside payments for performance
rubrics_metrics.description: You cannot receive anything of value from a non‑Government source for taking action or failing to take action in your Government position, nor accept payment for performing Federal duties from non‑Government sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include no honoraria for activities that are part of USPTO duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gifts — general rule regarding personal gifts from non‑Federal sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally you cannot accept gifts from anyone who has or is seeking business with or action from the Department, is regulated by Commerce, or has interests affected by your USPTO duties; gifts to family members because of relationship are considered gifts to you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Exceptions to the General Rule concerning Personal Gifts for allowable situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gifts — exceptions for personal gifts
rubrics_metrics.description: You may accept: gifts of $20 or less (other than cash/cash card) up to $50 per year; gifts from relatives/friends based on personal relationship; invitations to widely‑attended gatherings (with supervisor approval and subject to WAG rules); business meals overseas when a foreign person is present (in most cases); discounts generally available to the public; certain awards/honorary degrees; meals/lodging/travel based on outside business relationships or spouse’s employment; items of little intrinsic value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For political appointees, additional restrictions apply for gifts/invitations from registered lobbyists unless narrow exceptions are met; WAG defined by >100 persons (if not host) and value ≤ $415, and ethics official can adjudicate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gifts from foreign governments
rubrics_metrics.description: You may accept gifts from a foreign government of $415 or less; a gift over $415 can be accepted on behalf of the United States Government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gifts between employees — general rule
rubrics_metrics.description: You cannot offer a gift to a supervisor or accept a gift from a subordinate unless an exception applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions address special/infrequent major events and small token gifts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gifts between employees — exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowed exceptions include gifts for special infrequent major events (birth/adoption/recovery/retirement/wedding), food shared in the office, gifts worth $10 or less given occasionally, personal hospitality at one’s home, or gifts to a host/hostess (e.g., wine or flowers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Gifts to the Government — general rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Gifts to support agency activities may be accepted on behalf of USPTO with approval of an authorized official, but generally gifts from agency contractors/grantees, regulated industries (including companies/universities likely to seek a patent), or parties to controversial matters pending before the agency are disallowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gifts cannot be accepted if they would create an appearance of loss of impartiality; consult ethics official before seeking support for agency events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gifts for official travel
rubrics_metrics.description: You cannot ask anyone to pay for your travel; offers of travel payment may be accepted if they comply with gift standards, but you cannot accept first‑class tickets or an honorarium/speaking fee in connection with Government travel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms for reporting gifts and approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: Forms for reporting gifts and obtaining supervisor approval to accept invitations are available on the Commerce Ethics website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact ethics office or use www.commerce.gov/ethics for forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misuse of Government resources — general prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Government resources (funds, gift funds, equipment, supplies, services, duty time) are for authorized purposes only; you cannot use your USPTO title for personal activities or use nonpublic information learned on the job for personal purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Business contacts obtained through Federal employment cannot be used for personal benefit of yourself, friends, or relatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed limited uses of title, frequent flyer benefits, and internet/email
rubrics_metrics.description: You may use your USPTO title for personal biographical data and, with a disclaimer, when writing for scientific/technical publications; frequent flyer miles earned on Government travel may be used for personal purposes; Internet/email access and Government devices can be used for some personal activities subject to restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of title should include disclaimer; frequent flyer use is permitted even for personal upgrades; see Internet/email prohibited uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of internet and email — permitted and prohibited personal uses
rubrics_metrics.description: You can use Government internet/email and devices for personal activities if they do not interfere with office operations, are not prohibited by USPTO, and are not used for business/profit, political activities, lobbying, activities that incur extra charges to Government, discriminatory conduct, obtaining/viewing sexually explicit material, bringing discredit to the Department, or other statutory/regulatory violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office printers may be used for personal purposes if such use does not consume excessive resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seeking employment — disqualification upon job search
rubrics_metrics.description: Once you begin a job search, you must disqualify yourself from working on any matter affecting a prospective employer until you or the prospective employer ends discussions (or two months pass with no response after submitting a résumé); unsolicited résumé contacts impose a narrower disqualification limited to matters involving the employer individually until you receive a response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you are a political appointee who lobbied/served as foreign agent previously, special prohibitions on seeking employment with certain agencies may apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting employment contacts and discussions — required circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: You must report employment contacts/discussions in four situations: (1) if you are required to file public financial disclosure (SES, political appointee, SL/ST, OGE 278e) report contacts to an ethics official within three business days and state disqualification; (2) if participating in a procurement > $250,000 and contacted by competing contractors, notify ethics official and supervisor; (3) if you accept travel payments from a prospective employer, notify ethics official or supervisor in writing that you are disqualifying yourself; (4) if assigned a matter concerning a prospective employer, notify the assigner that you cannot work on it and it needs reassignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms and email reporting instructions are provided on Commerce Ethics website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post‑employment restrictions — general rules
rubrics_metrics.description: After leaving Federal service you generally cannot contact a Federal agency or court on behalf of someone else to influence Government action concerning a matter involving specific parties if you worked on it as a Government official, or for 2 years on matters that were under your responsibility during your last year; you cannot disclose/use protected nonpublic Federal information; and for 1 year you cannot obtain any patent or interest in any patent issued by USPTO (except by inheritance/bequest).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact an ethics official for case‑specific advice after leaving Government service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post‑employment restrictions for senior employees
rubrics_metrics.description: Senior employees (Executive Schedule pay or base pay ≥ $176,201) cannot, for 1 year, contact USPTO on behalf of someone else to influence Government action (with certain exceptions), or contact any branch of the U.S. Government on behalf of a foreign government or political party, or advise/assist a foreign government on dealings with the U.S. Government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post‑employment restrictions for senior political appointees
rubrics_metrics.description: Senior political appointees (Presidential appointees, Exec Schedule, base pay ≥ $176,201) cannot, for 2 years, contact USPTO (or entire Department if Director) or senior White House staff on behalf of someone else to influence Government action; cannot, for 2 years, engage in lobbying activities or activities requiring FARA registration before senior executive or military officials; and cannot, for 1 year, lobby or materially assist others to influence their former agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement officials and program managers — post‑employment compensation ban
rubrics_metrics.description: Procurement officials and program managers of procurements of $10,000,000 or more cannot, for 1 year, accept compensation from the bidder or contractor of the procurement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional post‑employment restrictions and attorney considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional restrictions apply to attorneys under bar rules and to former employees who received buyouts (restrictions on returning to Federal service within five years); former employees may contact an ethics official for advice after leaving service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial disclosure — who must file and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Presidential Appointees, SES members, non‑career policy‑making employees, procurement officials, and others whose duties could significantly affect public interests are required to file financial disclosure reports upon entry and annually thereafter; disclosures are used to advise and help avoid conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure accuracy and completeness; contact an ethics official for assistance in filling out reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial disclosure — required reporting details
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports must include specific holdings in IRAs, 401(k), trusts, or investment accounts (other than broadly diversified mutual funds if filing confidential OGE 450), a short description of activities/industry sector of privately‑held companies or limited partnerships, and assets/sources of income of spouse and dependent children.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transaction Reports for public filers
rubrics_metrics.description: If you file a public financial disclosure (OGE Form 278e) you must file a Transaction Report when you or your spouse/dependent child buy, sell, or exchange a security greater than $1,000; reports must be filed within 30 days of notice and no later than 45 days after the transaction date.
